topics.name: 1 Kings: overview
topics.description: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
evidence: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?

topics.name: Adonijah exalts himself and Solomon is anointed
topics.description: Adonijah declares he will be king, but Nathan and Bathsheba remind David of his oath, and David has Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon at Gihon. Adonijah flees to the altar and Solomon spares him on condition of good conduct.
evidence: Retell how Adonijah's attempt failed and Solomon was anointed
Name the people who stood with Adonijah and the people who did not
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Solomon became king instead of Adonijah?

topics.name: David's charge to Solomon and his death
topics.description: David, nearing death, tells Solomon to keep the LORD's commandments so the LORD will continue his word about David's house, and gives instructions about Joab, Barzillai's sons and Shimei. David dies after reigning forty years and Solomon sits on his throne.
evidence: Say what David told Solomon to do in order to walk with the LORD (2:3-4)
State how long David reigned and where he was buried
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what David charged Solomon with before he died?

topics.name: Solomon establishes his kingdom
topics.description: Solomon has Adonijah put to death after Adonijah asks for Abishag, removes Abiathar from the priesthood, has Joab killed at the altar, and puts Shimei to death when he leaves Jerusalem against his oath. The text concludes that the kingdom was established in Solomon's hand.
evidence: List the four men dealt with in chapter 2 and why each was judged
Find the verse that says the kingdom was established (2:46)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon dealt with Adonijah, Abiathar, Joab and Shimei?

topics.name: Solomon asks for wisdom at Gibeon
topics.description: At Gibeon the LORD appears to Solomon in a dream and says "Ask what I shall give thee"; Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people, and God also gives him riches and honour with a call to walk in his ways.
evidence: Say what Solomon asked for and what God added
Explain why the LORD was pleased with the request (3:10-11)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked God for at Gibeon, and what God gave him?

topics.name: Solomon judges between two mothers
topics.description: Two women claim the same living child; Solomon orders the child divided, and the mother whose heart yearns for her son is revealed. All Israel sees the wisdom of God in him.
evidence: Retell how Solomon found the real mother
Say what Israel concluded about Solomon (3:28)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of the two mothers and say what it shows about Solomon's wisdom?

topics.name: Solomon's officials, provisions and fame
topics.description: Chapter 4 lists Solomon's officials and twelve district officers, describes Israel dwelling safely and his wide dominion, and records his wisdom, proverbs and songs and the visitors who came to hear him.
evidence: Name the picture of peace in 4:25
Give two ways the chapter shows Solomon's wisdom or fame (4:29-34)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how 1 Kings 4 shows God keeping his word to give Solomon wisdom?

topics.name: Solomon and Hiram prepare to build the temple
topics.description: Solomon tells Hiram of Tyre that David could not build the house because of his wars, but that the LORD has given rest; Hiram supplies cedar and fir for wheat and oil, and Solomon raises a levy of workers.
evidence: Say why David had not built the house (5:3)
Describe the agreement between Solomon and Hiram
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, built the house of the LORD?

topics.name: Solomon builds the temple
topics.description: The house of the LORD is built in seven and a half years of work with stone, cedar and gold, with an inner oracle holding two cherubim. In the middle of the building the LORD tells Solomon that if he keeps the statutes, God will dwell among Israel.
evidence: Say what was in the inner room (the oracle) and what covered the house
State the condition and promise in 6:12-13
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the temple Solomon built and what the LORD said to him about it?

topics.name: Solomon's palace and the temple furnishings
topics.description: Solomon builds his own house over thirteen years, and Hiram of Tyre casts the two bronze pillars, the molten sea, bases, lavers and other vessels for the temple.
evidence: Name some of the bronze items Hiram made
Say how long Solomon took to build his own house (7:1)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name some furnishings made for the temple and who made them?

topics.name: The ark is brought into the temple and the glory fills it
topics.description: At the feast Solomon and the elders bring the ark of the covenant into the oracle; there is nothing in it but the two tables of stone, and a cloud fills the house so the priests cannot minister.
evidence: Say what the ark contained (8:9)
Describe what happened when the priests came out (8:10-11)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was brought into the new temple?

topics.name: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the LORD's word to David
topics.description: Solomon blesses the LORD for keeping what he spoke to David his father, that David's son would build the house, and says the place is set for the ark with the covenant the LORD made with Israel's fathers.
evidence: Say what the LORD promised David about the house (8:18-19)
Explain how Solomon says the promise was kept (8:20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon says the LORD had spoken to David about building the house?

topics.name: Solomon's prayer of dedication
topics.description: Standing before the altar, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be confirmed, and prays that God will hear and forgive in specific situations of sin, defeat, famine, a stranger's prayer and exile.
evidence: Say what Solomon asks God to do when his people sin and then repent (8:33-34, 46-50)
Find where Solomon asks God to keep his word to David (8:25-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's dedication prayer and what he asks for?

topics.name: Solomon blesses the people and the feast ends
topics.description: Solomon blesses the congregation, urges their hearts to be perfect with the LORD, and the king and all Israel offer great sacrifices and keep a feast before sending the people home joyful.
evidence: Say what Solomon urged the people to do (8:61)
Describe how the people went home (8:66)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the dedication of the temple ended?

topics.name: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time
topics.description: The LORD says he has hallowed the house and promises to establish Solomon's throne for ever as he promised David if Solomon walks in integrity, but warns that if Israel and their children turn away he will cut Israel off and cast out the house.
evidence: State the promise and the warning (9:4-7)
Say what the nations would conclude if Israel forsook the LORD (9:8-9)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the conditions the LORD set before Solomon after the temple was finished?

topics.name: Solomon's cities, labour and ships
topics.description: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities, raises a levy to build the temple, his house and cities, puts the remaining Canaanite peoples to forced labour, offers sacrifices three times a year, and builds a fleet that brings gold from Ophir.
evidence: Name some things built with the levy (9:15-19)
Say where the fleet gold came from (9:26-28)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon used his labour force and wealth after the temple was built?

topics.name: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon
topics.description: The queen of Sheba comes to test Solomon with hard questions, sees his wisdom and house, and blesses the LORD who set him on the throne. The chapter also records Solomon's great gold, ivory throne, chariots and horses.
evidence: Say what the queen concluded after seeing Solomon (10:6-9)
Name some signs of Solomon's wealth in the chapter
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and what she said about the LORD?

topics.name: Solomon's heart turns away
topics.description: Solomon loves many foreign wives from nations the LORD had forbidden, his wives turn his heart to other gods, and he builds high places. The LORD tells him he will tear the kingdom away, though not in his days and not all of it, for David's sake.
evidence: Say what turned Solomon's heart (11:3-4)
State what the LORD said would happen and what he would hold back (11:11-13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was angry with Solomon and what he said would follow?

topics.name: Adversaries and Jeroboam's promise
topics.description: The LORD raises up Hadad the Edomite and Rezon of Damascus against Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah tears his garment in twelve pieces and tells Jeroboam he will rule ten tribes if he walks in the LORD's ways. Solomon seeks to kill Jeroboam, who flees to Egypt, and Solomon dies after forty years.
evidence: Name the adversaries raised up against Solomon
Explain what the torn garment pictured (11:29-31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe Ahijah's sign to Jeroboam and what it meant?

topics.name: The kingdom divides at Shechem
topics.description: Rehoboam rejects the old men's counsel and answers Israel harshly; ten tribes break away and make Jeroboam king while Judah stays with Rehoboam. The text says the cause was from the LORD, and Shemaiah forbids war against their brethren.
evidence: Compare the counsel of the old men and the young men (12:7, 10-11)
Say which tribes followed Rehoboam and which followed Jeroboam
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the kingdom of Israel was divided after Solomon?

topics.name: Jeroboam makes golden calves at Bethel and Dan
topics.description: Fearing his people will return to Rehoboam if they go to Jerusalem, Jeroboam makes two golden calves, sets them in Bethel and Dan, appoints priests who were not Levites and ordains a feast. The text says this thing became a sin.
evidence: Say why Jeroboam made the calves (12:26-27)
List the changes he made to Israel's worship
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jeroboam did at Bethel and Dan and why it was sin?

topics.name: The man of God from Judah and the old prophet
topics.description: A man of God from Judah cries against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, naming a child Josiah, and the altar is rent. He is told not to eat or drink there, but is deceived by an old prophet and killed by a lion on the way home.
evidence: Retell how the man of God disobeyed and what happened
Say what the sign at the altar was (13:3-5)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell the story of the man of God who came from Judah to Bethel?

topics.name: Ahijah announces judgment on Jeroboam's house
topics.description: Jeroboam's wife, disguised, goes to Ahijah about her sick son; Ahijah tells her the LORD will cut off Jeroboam's house and root up Israel from the land because of his sins. The chapter then reports Jeroboam's death and Rehoboam's evil reign in Judah, including Shishak's raid on Jerusalem.
evidence: Say what Ahijah announced about Jeroboam's house (14:10-16)
Name what Shishak of Egypt took from Jerusalem (14:25-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD said through Ahijah about Jeroboam and about Israel?

topics.name: Abijam and Asa reign in Judah
topics.description: Abijam walks in his father's sins, yet for David's sake the LORD gives him a lamp in Jerusalem. Asa does right as David did, removes idols and his mother Maachah from being queen, but the high places stay; he pays Benhadad of Syria to break with Baasha of Israel.
evidence: Say what Asa removed and what he left (15:12-14)
Explain how Asa dealt with Baasha's building of Ramah (15:17-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Asa served the LORD and where he fell short?

topics.name: Nadab and Baasha, kings of Israel
topics.description: Nadab of Israel walks in Jeroboam's sin and Baasha kills him and all of Jeroboam's house. The LORD then speaks through Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha for walking in Jeroboam's way.
evidence: Say how Jeroboam's house ended (15:29-30)
State the word of the LORD against Baasha (16:2-4)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the house of Jeroboam ended, and why Baasha was judged too?

topics.name: Elah, Zimri and Omri
topics.description: Zimri kills Elah and Baasha's house, reigns seven days and burns the palace when Omri besieges Tirzah; Israel divides between Tibni and Omri, and Omri prevails, buys the hill of Samaria and does worse than all before him.
evidence: Say how Zimri's reign ended (16:15-19)
Name the city Omri built and what he did in the LORD's sight (16:24-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} follow the quick succession of Elah, Zimri and Omri in Israel?

topics.name: Ahab begins to reign
topics.description: Ahab son of Omri does evil above all before him, marries Jezebel daughter of the king of the Zidonians, serves Baal and builds an altar for Baal in Samaria. The chapter ends with Hiel building Jericho at the cost of his sons.
evidence: Name three things that made Ahab worse than earlier kings (16:30-33)
Say who Ahab married
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say what kind of king Ahab was and who his wife was?

topics.name: Elijah announces drought and is fed by ravens
topics.description: Elijah the Tishbite tells Ahab there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word, and the LORD sends him to hide by the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him bread and flesh until the brook dries up.
evidence: Say what Elijah told Ahab (17:1)
Explain how the LORD fed Elijah at Cherith
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how God provided for Elijah by the brook Cherith?

topics.name: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath
topics.description: The LORD sends Elijah to a widow at Zarephath with only a handful of meal and a little oil; at his word she feeds him first, and the barrel and cruse do not run out.
evidence: Retell what the widow had and what happened to it
Say whose word the meal and oil followed (17:14, 16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the widow's meal and oil, and why?

topics.name: The widow's son is raised
topics.description: The widow's son falls sick and dies; Elijah prays and stretches himself on the child, the LORD hears and the child revives. The woman says she now knows Elijah is a man of God and the LORD's word in his mouth is truth.
evidence: Retell what Elijah did and prayed
Say what the widow confessed at the end (17:24)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the widow's son was brought back to life and what she said?

topics.name: Elijah meets Obadiah and Ahab
topics.description: In the third year of the famine the LORD sends Elijah to show himself to Ahab; Obadiah, who feared the LORD and hid a hundred prophets from Jezebel, brings word. Elijah tells Ahab that he and his father's house have troubled Israel by forsaking the LORD, and calls for a gathering on Carmel.
evidence: Say what Obadiah did for the LORD's prophets (18:4)
State who Elijah said had troubled Israel (18:17-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab when they met?

topics.name: The LORD answers by fire on Mount Carmel
topics.description: Elijah challenges the people to choose between the LORD and Baal and sets a test: the God who answers by fire is God. Baal's prophets cry out all day without answer; Elijah's drenched sacrifice is consumed by the fire of the LORD, and the people declare that the LORD is God.
evidence: Retell the contest and its result
Say what the people cried when the fire fell (18:39)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain the contest on Carmel and what it proved?

topics.name: The rain returns
topics.description: Elijah tells Ahab to eat, because there is the sound of abundance of rain; after he prays and his servant looks seven times, a small cloud rises and heavy rain falls.
evidence: Say what Elijah's servant saw on the seventh look (18:44)
Explain what this ended (compare 17:1)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the drought ended in Elijah's day?

topics.name: Elijah flees from Jezebel
topics.description: Jezebel vows to kill Elijah, and he flees to the wilderness and asks to die under a juniper tree; an angel touches him and feeds him, and he walks forty days and nights to Horeb.
evidence: Say what led Elijah to flee (19:1-3)
Describe how the LORD cared for him (19:5-8)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah ran away, and how God cared for him?

topics.name: The LORD speaks to Elijah at Horeb
topics.description: At Horeb Elijah complains that he alone is left; the LORD is not in the wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice, and sends him to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, saying he has left seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal.
evidence: Describe the wind, earthquake, fire and voice
State the three people Elijah was told to anoint and the number left in Israel
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Elijah at Horeb and how he spoke?

topics.name: Elijah calls Elisha
topics.description: Elijah finds Elisha son of Shaphat ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen and casts his mantle on him; Elisha slaughters a yoke of oxen, boils the flesh, takes leave of his parents and follows Elijah.
evidence: Say what Elijah did to call Elisha (19:19)
Say what Elisha did before following
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Elisha was called to follow Elijah?

topics.name: Israel defeats Benhadad at Samaria
topics.description: Benhadad of Syria and thirty-two kings demand Ahab's silver, gold and family; a prophet tells Ahab the LORD will deliver the host into his hand by the young men of the provincial princes, and Israel wins.
evidence: Say what the prophet promised and why (20:13)
Describe how the battle went (20:15-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Israel beat the Syrian army at Samaria?

topics.name: Aphek and Ahab spares Benhadad
topics.description: The Syrians say the LORD is a god of the hills, so the LORD gives Israel victory on the plain at Aphek; Ahab then makes a covenant with Benhadad and lets him go. A prophet, disguised, tells Ahab that for letting go the man the LORD appointed to destruction, his life will go for Benhadad's life.
evidence: Say what the Syrians said about the LORD and what the LORD answered (20:23, 28)
Explain the prophet's message to Ahab (20:42)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD was displeased when Ahab let Benhadad go?

topics.name: Naboth's vineyard
topics.description: Ahab wants Naboth's vineyard, but Naboth will not give his fathers' inheritance; Jezebel arranges false witnesses so Naboth is stoned and Ahab takes the vineyard.
evidence: Say why Naboth refused (21:3)
Describe what Jezebel did to get the vineyard
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how Ahab and Jezebel took Naboth's vineyard, and what was wrong with it?

topics.name: Elijah pronounces judgment on Ahab
topics.description: The LORD sends Elijah to Ahab in Naboth's vineyard: Ahab's house will be cut off like Jeroboam's and Baasha's and the dogs will eat Jezebel. Ahab tears his clothes and humbles himself, and the LORD says the evil will not come in his days but in his son's.
evidence: State the judgment on Ahab and on Jezebel (21:21-24)
Say how the LORD responded when Ahab humbled himself (21:27-29)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Elijah told Ahab about Naboth's vineyard and what happened when Ahab humbled himself?

topics.name: Micaiah prophesies against Ahab
topics.description: Ahab asks Jehoshaphat to join him at Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying the LORD's word, describes Israel scattered as sheep without a shepherd and a lying spirit in the prophets' mouths. Ahab puts Micaiah in prison.
evidence: Compare the four hundred prophets and Micaiah
Say what Ahab did with Micaiah (22:26-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat wanted to hear a prophet of the LORD and what Micaiah said?

topics.name: Ahab dies at Ramoth-gilead
topics.description: Ahab disguises himself in battle but a man draws a bow at random and strikes him; he dies, and the dogs lick his blood as the LORD had said.
evidence: Say how Ahab tried to avoid Micaiah's word and what happened
Find the verse that says his death was according to the LORD's word (22:38)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Ahab died and how it matched what the LORD said?

topics.name: Jehoshaphat of Judah and Ahaziah of Israel
topics.description: Jehoshaphat walks in the ways of Asa and does right, though the high places remain; his ships to Ophir are broken. Ahaziah son of Ahab reigns in Israel, serving Baal as his father did.
evidence: Say how Jehoshaphat is described (22:43)
Say how Ahaziah is described (22:52-53)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} compare Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah as the book of 1 Kings ends?

topics.name: 2 Kings: overview
topics.description: 2 Kings continues the divided kingdom from Ahaziah of Israel through Elijah and Elisha, the end of the house of Ahab, the fall of Samaria and the exile of Israel (ch. 17), the kings of Judah including Hezekiah and Josiah, and the exile of Judah to Babylon (ch. 25).
evidence: Name the two kingdoms and say how each ends (ch. 17 and ch. 25)
Name Elijah, Elisha, Hezekiah and Josiah and where they appear
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline 2 Kings in order, from Elijah's last days to the exile in Babylon?

topics.name: Ahaziah consults Baal-zebub and fire falls
topics.description: Ahaziah, hurt in a fall, sends to ask Baal-zebub god of Ekron whether he will recover; Elijah meets the messengers and says he will die because there is a God in Israel. Fire from heaven consumes two captains of fifty, and Elijah goes with the third.
evidence: Say why Ahaziah was told he would die (1:3-4, 16)
Retell what happened to the captains of fifty
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why Elijah sent Ahaziah this message and what happened to the soldiers?

topics.name: Elijah is taken up and Elisha receives his mantle
topics.description: Elijah and Elisha cross Jordan, Elisha asks for a double portion of Elijah's spirit, and Elijah is taken up by a whirlwind with a chariot of fire. Elisha takes up the fallen mantle, strikes the Jordan and crosses, and the sons of the prophets say the spirit of Elijah rests on him.
evidence: Describe how Elijah left and what Elisha picked up
Say what the sons of the prophets recognised (2:15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah left the earth and who took up his work?

topics.name: Elisha heals the spring and the boys mock him
topics.description: At Jericho Elisha casts salt into the spring and the waters are healed, according to his word; going up to Bethel, small boys mock him and two she bears tear forty-two of them after he curses them in the LORD's name.
evidence: Say what Elisha did to the waters at Jericho and by whose word
Describe what happened at Bethel (2:23-24)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did at Jericho and what happened on the road to Bethel?

topics.name: Three kings and Moab: water in the valley
topics.description: Jehoram of Israel, Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom march against rebel Moab and run out of water; Elisha, for Jehoshaphat's sake, says the LORD will fill the valley and give Moab into their hand. Water comes by morning and Moab is defeated, though the king of Moab offers his eldest son on the wall.
evidence: Say why Elisha agreed to inquire of the LORD (3:13-14)
Describe how the water came (3:16-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD provided for the three kings, and why Elisha helped?

topics.name: Elisha and the widow's oil
topics.description: A prophet's widow cries to Elisha because a creditor will take her two sons; Elisha tells her to borrow empty vessels and pour from her small pot of oil, and the oil flows until all the vessels are full, so she sells it and pays her debt.
evidence: Say what the widow had in the house and what happened to it
Say what she did with the oil afterwards (4:7)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how Elisha helped the widow pay her debt?

topics.name: The Shunammite woman's son
topics.description: A woman of Shunem builds a room for Elisha and, as he promised, bears a son; when the boy later dies, she goes to Elisha at Carmel, and Elisha prays, stretches himself on the child, and the boy sneezes and opens his eyes.
evidence: Say what the woman did for Elisha and what he promised her
Describe how Elisha restored the child
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how the Shunammite's son was brought back to life?

topics.name: Death in the pot and the loaves
topics.description: In a famine at Gilgal, wild gourds make the stew deadly and Elisha casts in meal so it is harmless; he then has a hundred men fed from twenty loaves, with some left, according to the LORD's word.
evidence: Say how Elisha made the pottage safe
Say what the LORD said about the twenty loaves (4:43)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did for the sons of the prophets during the famine?

topics.name: Naaman is healed of leprosy
topics.description: Naaman, the Syrian commander, hears from an Israelite servant girl of the prophet in Samaria, goes to Elisha and is told to wash seven times in Jordan; he is angry but obeys and is healed, and confesses there is no God in all the earth but in Israel. Gehazi takes a reward by deceit and Naaman's leprosy comes on him.
evidence: Retell why Naaman was angry and what changed his mind
Say what happened to Gehazi and why (5:20-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell the story of Naaman, the servant girl and Gehazi?

topics.name: The iron axe head floats
topics.description: While the sons of the prophets cut beams at Jordan, a borrowed axe head falls into the water; Elisha casts in a stick and the iron swims, and the man takes it up.
evidence: Say what Elisha threw into the water and what happened
Say why the man was distressed (6:5)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell what happened to the borrowed axe head?

topics.name: Elisha and the Syrian army at Dothan
topics.description: The king of Syria sends an army to take Elisha at Dothan; Elisha's servant sees them, Elisha prays and the servant sees chariots of fire around the mountain. The Syrians are struck blind, led to Samaria, given food and sent home, and the bands of Syria stop coming into Israel.
evidence: Say what the servant saw when his eyes were opened (6:17)
Explain how Elisha told the king of Israel to treat the Syrians (6:21-23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha's servant saw at Dothan and how the story ended?

topics.name: Famine in besieged Samaria
topics.description: Benhadad besieges Samaria, a great famine follows and the king of Israel, hearing a woman's terrible plea, tears his clothes and swears to take Elisha's head; Elisha tells the elders the king's messenger is coming.
evidence: Describe the state of the city (6:25)
Say what the king blamed and decided (6:31, 33)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the famine in Samaria and how the king reacted?

topics.name: The LORD lifts the siege of Samaria
topics.description: Elisha says that by tomorrow fine flour will sell for a shekel at the gate; four lepers find the Syrian camp empty because the LORD made the Syrians hear the noise of a great host, and the city is plundered. The lord who doubted sees it but dies in the gate trampled by the crowd.
evidence: Say what Elisha prophesied (7:1) and how it happened
Say what happened to the doubting lord (7:17-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the siege of Samaria ended and how Elisha's word came true?

topics.name: The Shunammite's land and Elisha at Damascus
topics.description: Elisha warns the Shunammite of a seven-year famine; on her return the king hears about Elisha's deeds from Gehazi and restores her land. Elisha later tells Hazael he will be king of Syria and do great evil to Israel, and Hazael kills Benhadad.
evidence: Say what the king restored to the woman and why (8:4-6)
Say what Elisha told Hazael and how Elisha reacted (8:12)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the Shunammite woman after the famine, and what Elisha said to Hazael?

topics.name: Jehoram and Ahaziah of Judah
topics.description: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat marries a daughter of Ahab and does evil, yet the LORD will not destroy Judah for David's sake, as he promised David a light for his children. Edom revolts; his son Ahaziah walks in the way of Ahab's house and goes with Joram of Israel to fight Hazael at Ramoth-gilead.
evidence: Say why the LORD did not destroy Judah (8:19)
Say how Jehoram and Ahaziah are compared to the house of Ahab (8:18, 27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why God spared Judah despite Jehoram's evil?

topics.name: Jehu is anointed king over Israel
topics.description: Elisha sends a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to pour oil on Jehu's head and announce that he will strike the house of Ahab, and that dogs will eat Jezebel; the captains acclaim Jehu king.
evidence: Say what Jehu was told to do (9:6-10)
Describe how the other captains responded (9:13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Jehu was anointed and what he was told to do?

topics.name: Jehu strikes Joram and Ahaziah
topics.description: Jehu drives to Jezreel and shoots Joram, throwing him into Naboth's field according to the LORD's word; Ahaziah of Judah flees and is killed too.
evidence: Say where Joram died and why Jehu cited Naboth (9:25-26)
Say what happened to Ahaziah of Judah
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Joram and Ahaziah were killed?

topics.name: The death of Jezebel
topics.description: Jehu enters Jezreel; Jezebel is thrown from the window, trampled, and the dogs eat her, so that Jehu says it is the word of the LORD spoken by Elijah.
evidence: Say how Jezebel died and what remained
Find the verse that links her death to Elijah's word (9:36)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Elijah's word about Jezebel came true?

topics.name: Jehu destroys the house of Ahab and the worship of Baal
topics.description: Jehu has Ahab's seventy sons killed in Samaria, kills Ahaziah's brethren and the remainder of Ahab's house, then gathers the worshippers of Baal in the house of Baal and has them slain, destroying the house and image of Baal.
evidence: Say how Jehu summoned the worshippers of Baal and what he did
Say whose word Jehu says is fulfilled (10:10)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Jehu did to Ahab's house and to Baal worship in Israel?

topics.name: Jehu's reign and its limits
topics.description: The LORD tells Jehu that his sons to the fourth generation will sit on Israel's throne, but Jehu does not depart from Jeroboam's calves or walk in the law with all his heart, and the LORD begins to cut Israel short by Hazael.
evidence: Say what the LORD promised Jehu and what Jehu failed to do (10:30-31)
Say who began to cut Israel short (10:32)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain both the promise to Jehu and where he fell short?

topics.name: Athaliah and the hidden king Joash
topics.description: After Ahaziah's death Athaliah destroys the royal seed and reigns six years; Jehosheba hides the baby Joash in the house of the LORD, and in the seventh year Jehoiada anoints him, Athaliah is put to death, and Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the king and the people.
evidence: Say how Joash was saved and for how long he was hidden
Say what the covenant of Jehoiada was (11:17)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how young Joash became king of Judah?

topics.name: Joash repairs the temple
topics.description: Joash does right while Jehoiada instructs him, though the high places stay; when the priests have not repaired the house by his twenty-third year, a chest is placed at the altar and the money repairs it. Hazael threatens Jerusalem and Joash is killed by his servants.
evidence: Say how the temple money was collected and used (12:9-15)
Say how Joash's reign ended (12:17-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joash arranged the repair of the temple?

topics.name: Jehoahaz and Joash of Israel
topics.description: Jehoahaz of Israel follows Jeroboam's sins, so the LORD delivers Israel into Hazael's hand; when Jehoahaz seeks the LORD, he gives Israel a saviour, yet they do not depart from Jeroboam's sins. His son Joash reigns in the same way.
evidence: Say what happened when Jehoahaz sought the LORD (13:4-5)
Say whether Israel turned from Jeroboam's sins (13:6)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how the LORD treated Israel under Jehoahaz?

topics.name: Elisha's last word and death
topics.description: The dying Elisha has King Joash shoot an arrow of the LORD's deliverance from Syria and strike the ground; Joash strikes only three times, so Elisha says he will defeat Syria only three times. After Elisha's death a dead man touches his bones and revives; the LORD is gracious to Israel because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
evidence: Describe the arrows and why Elisha was angry (13:17-19)
Find the verse that names the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (13:23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Elisha did on his deathbed and why the LORD still showed Israel compassion?

topics.name: Amaziah of Judah
topics.description: Amaziah does right, though not like David, kills the servants who killed his father but spares their children as the law of Moses says, defeats Edom, then challenges Joash of Israel and is beaten at Beth-shemesh, with Jerusalem's wall broken and the temple treasures taken. He is later killed in a conspiracy.
evidence: Say what Amaziah did and did not do with the children of the murderers (14:5-6)
Describe the result of his challenge to Israel (14:11-14)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe Amaziah's reign, including his pride in challenging Israel?

topics.name: Jeroboam II of Israel
topics.description: Jeroboam son of Joash does evil like the earlier kings, yet restores Israel's border according to the word spoken by Jonah the prophet, because the LORD saw Israel's bitter affliction and had not said he would blot out Israel's name.
evidence: Name the prophet mentioned in 14:25
Say why the LORD saved Israel by Jeroboam (14:26-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD helped Israel by Jeroboam II even though he did evil?

topics.name: Azariah and Jotham of Judah
topics.description: Azariah (Uzziah) does right, but the high places remain and the LORD smites him with leprosy until his death; his son Jotham does right in the same way. In Jotham's days the LORD begins to send Rezin of Syria and Pekah against Judah.
evidence: Say what happened to Azariah and where he lived (15:5)
Say what remained in Judah despite the kings doing right (15:4, 35)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the reigns of Azariah and Jotham?

topics.name: Israel's last kings: Zachariah to Pekah
topics.description: Zachariah, Shallum, Menahem, Pekahiah and Pekah rule Israel in quick succession, mostly by conspiracy, all doing evil; Pul of Assyria is paid off by Menahem and Tiglath-pileser takes cities and carries people captive in Pekah's days. Hoshea then kills Pekah.
evidence: Say how Zachariah's end fulfilled the word to Jehu (15:12)
Say how Assyria begins to affect Israel (15:19, 29)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Assyria began to take Israel's land and people?

topics.name: Ahaz of Judah turns to Assyria
topics.description: Ahaz walks in the way of Israel's kings, burns his son in the fire and sacrifices at the high places. Rezin and Pekah besiege Jerusalem, and Ahaz sends the temple silver and gold to Tiglath-pileser; he then copies a Damascus altar and moves the LORD's bronze altar aside.
evidence: Say who Ahaz asked for help and what he paid (16:7-8)
Describe what he did with the altar at the temple (16:10-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Ahaz did instead of trusting the LORD when Syria and Israel attacked?

topics.name: Samaria falls to Assyria
topics.description: Hoshea becomes Assyria's servant, then conspires with Egypt; Shalmaneser besieges Samaria, takes it in Hoshea's ninth year and carries Israel into Assyria.
evidence: Say what Hoshea did that led to the siege (17:4)
Say where Israel was carried (17:6)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how and when the northern kingdom of Israel was taken captive?

topics.name: Why the LORD removed Israel
topics.description: The writer explains that Israel sinned against the LORD who brought them from Egypt, walked in the nations' ways, ignored the prophets, rejected his covenant and statutes, and followed Jeroboam's sin, so the LORD removed them. Judah also did not keep his commandments.
evidence: List several sins named in 17:7-17
Say how the LORD had warned them (17:13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} give the reasons 2 Kings 17 gives for Israel's exile?

topics.name: Foreign peoples settled in Samaria
topics.description: The king of Assyria brings peoples from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath and Sepharvaim to Samaria; lions come among them until a priest taught the manner of the God of the land, but each nation keeps its own gods while also fearing the LORD.
evidence: Say how the settlers came to fear the LORD (17:25-28)
Say why the writer says they did not truly fear the LORD (17:34-41)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened in the land after Israel was taken away?

topics.name: Hezekiah trusts the LORD
topics.description: Hezekiah does right as David did, removes the high places and breaks the bronze serpent Moses made, which Israel had been burning incense to, and trusts the LORD like no king before or after him. He rebels against Assyria.
evidence: Say what Hezekiah removed and what he did to the bronze serpent (18:4)
Say what the writer says about his trust in the LORD (18:5-7)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe what made Hezekiah a good king?

topics.name: Sennacherib's officer taunts Jerusalem
topics.description: Sennacherib takes Judah's fortified cities and Hezekiah pays him; the king of Assyria still sends Rabshakeh, who mocks Hezekiah's trust in the LORD and Egypt and tells the people not to listen to him, asking which gods have delivered their land.
evidence: Say what Rabshakeh told the people on the wall (18:28-35)
Say how the people responded (18:36)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Rabshakeh said to shake Judah's trust in the LORD?

topics.name: The LORD delivers Jerusalem
topics.description: Hezekiah spreads Sennacherib's letter before the LORD and prays; Isaiah says the LORD will defend the city for his own sake and David's sake, and that night the angel of the LORD strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib returns to Nineveh and is killed by his sons.
evidence: Retell Hezekiah's prayer and what he asked (19:15-19)
Say what happened to the Assyrian army (19:35)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how God answered Hezekiah's prayer against Sennacherib?

topics.name: Hezekiah's illness and the Babylonian envoys
topics.description: Hezekiah is told by Isaiah he will die, prays, and the LORD adds fifteen years, giving the shadow going back ten degrees as a sign. Afterward he shows Babylon's envoys all his treasures, and Isaiah tells him all will be carried to Babylon; Hezekiah says the word is good.
evidence: Say what sign the LORD gave and what he promised (20:5-11)
Say what Isaiah foretold about Babylon (20:16-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD did when Hezekiah was sick, and what Isaiah said about Babylon?

topics.name: Manasseh and Amon
topics.description: Manasseh rebuilds the high places, sets altars for the host of heaven in the LORD's house, passes his son through the fire and sheds much innocent blood; the LORD announces evil on Jerusalem like Samaria's. His son Amon does the same and is killed by his servants.
evidence: List some of Manasseh's sins (21:3-6, 16)
Say what the LORD announced would happen to Jerusalem (21:12-15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Manasseh led Judah further into sin, and what the LORD announced?

topics.name: Josiah and the book of the law
topics.description: In Josiah's eighteenth year, repairs to the temple turn up the book of the law; the king tears his clothes at its words, and Huldah the prophetess says the evil will come on Jerusalem but not in Josiah's days because his heart was tender.
evidence: Say what Hilkiah found and how Josiah reacted (22:8-11)
Say what Huldah told Josiah (22:16-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what happened when the book of the law was found in the temple?

topics.name: Josiah renews the covenant and cleanses the land
topics.description: Josiah reads the book of the covenant to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to walk after him; he removes idols and high places in Judah, defiles Topheth, and at Bethel breaks Jeroboam's altar and burns bones on it according to the word of the man of God.
evidence: Say what Josiah covenanted (23:3)
Describe what he did at Bethel and which earlier prophecy it matched (23:15-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Josiah renewed the covenant and what he removed?

topics.name: Josiah's Passover and the verdict on Judah
topics.description: Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover as written; no such Passover had been held since the judges. No king before or after turned to the LORD as he did, yet the LORD did not turn from his wrath because of Manasseh, and says he will remove Judah as he removed Israel.
evidence: Say how the Passover was different (23:22)
Say why the LORD did not turn from his wrath (23:26-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD still would not turn from his anger after Josiah's reforms?

topics.name: Josiah's death and Jehoahaz and Jehoiakim
topics.description: Josiah dies at Megiddo when Pharaoh-nechoh goes up to Assyria; Jehoahaz reigns three months and is taken to Egypt, and Pharaoh makes Eliakim king as Jehoiakim, who taxes the land to pay him.
evidence: Say how Josiah died (23:29-30)
Say who appointed Jehoiakim (23:34)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Judah's kings right after Josiah?

topics.name: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin
topics.description: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar, then rebels, and the LORD sends bands against Judah as he said by the prophets because of Manasseh's sin; his son Jehoiachin surrenders to Babylon and Nebuchadnezzar carries off the temple treasures and about ten thousand captives. He appoints Zedekiah king.
evidence: Say why the LORD sent the invaders (24:2-4)
Say what Nebuchadnezzar took and who he made king (24:13-17)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Babylon took the first captives from Judah?

topics.name: The fall of Jerusalem
topics.description: Zedekiah rebels and Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem; the city is broken up, Zedekiah is blinded after his sons are killed, and the Chaldeans burn the temple, palace and houses, break the walls and carry off the temple's bronze and the people.
evidence: Describe what happened to Zedekiah and to the temple
Say how Judah's exile is summed up (25:21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how and why Jerusalem was destroyed?

topics.name: Gedaliah and Jehoiachin's release
topics.description: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah over the people left in Judah, but Ishmael kills him and the people flee to Egypt. The book ends with Evil-merodach lifting Jehoiachin out of prison in Babylon and giving him a daily allowance.
evidence: Say what happened to Gedaliah (25:25)
Say how the book of 2 Kings ends (25:27-30)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how 2 Kings ends and who was released from prison?

topics.name: 1 Chronicles: overview
topics.description: 1 Chronicles opens with genealogies from Adam to the returned exiles (chs. 1-9), tells of Saul's death and David's reign (chs. 10-21), and then David's preparations for the temple, the organising of Levites and officers, and the accession of Solomon (chs. 22-29).
evidence: Name the three parts: genealogies, David's reign, preparations for the temple
Say how the book begins (Adam) and ends (David's death and Solomon reigning)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline 1 Chronicles in order, from the genealogies to David's death?

topics.name: Genealogies from Adam to Israel
topics.description: 1 Chronicles 1 lists the line from Adam to Noah's sons, the nations from Japheth, Ham and Shem, the line to Abraham, Abraham's sons through Ishmael, Keturah and Isaac, and Esau's descendants and the kings of Edom.
evidence: Say whose name begins the list (1:1) and whose sons are named in 1:34
Say which sons of Isaac are traced (1:34)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say where 1 Chronicles begins its list of names and why a book of history might start there?

topics.name: The twelve sons of Israel and the line of Judah
topics.description: Chapter 2 names the twelve sons of Israel and then follows Judah in detail through Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon and Jesse to David, with other branches of Judah's families.
evidence: List the twelve sons of Israel as named in 2:1-2
Say whose name ends the main line in 2:13-15
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} follow the line from Judah to David in 1 Chronicles 2?

topics.name: David's sons and the line of the kings of Judah
topics.description: Chapter 3 lists David's sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem, then follows Solomon's line through the kings of Judah to the exile and the descendants of Jehoiachin.
evidence: Say where David's sons were born and how long he reigned in each place (3:4)
Name some of the kings in the line from Solomon (3:10-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 3 traces from David to the exile?

topics.name: Other families of Judah and Simeon, and Jabez
topics.description: Chapter 4 lists further families of Judah and Simeon. In the middle the text singles out Jabez, honoured above his brothers, who called on the God of Israel for blessing and was granted what he asked.
evidence: Say what Jabez asked of God and the result (4:10)
Name the two tribes whose families are listed
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what is said about Jabez in 1 Chronicles 4?

topics.name: Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
topics.description: Chapter 5 explains that Reuben lost the birthright to Joseph, lists Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh east of Jordan, notes that they cried to God and were helped in battle, and says they sinned by following other gods and were carried away by Assyria.
evidence: Say what happened to Reuben's birthright (5:1-2)
Say why the eastern tribes were carried away (5:25-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles 5 says the eastern tribes were taken captive?

topics.name: The tribe of Levi: priests and singers
topics.description: Chapter 6 traces Levi through Gershon, Kohath and Merari, the line of the high priests, the Levitical towns, and the singers David set over the service of song, Heman, Asaph and Ethan.
evidence: Name the three sons of Levi (6:1)
Say what David set the singers over (6:31-32)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say who the priests and singers were according to 1 Chronicles 6?

topics.name: Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim and Asher
topics.description: Chapter 7 lists families of several tribes, noting their numbers of mighty men of valour, and ends with Asher.
evidence: Name some tribes in the chapter
Say what the writer counts for several tribes
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name some of the tribes covered in 1 Chronicles 7?

topics.name: Benjamin and the house of Saul
topics.description: Chapter 8 lists Benjamin's families, and 8:33-40 traces Saul and his sons; the same line is repeated in 9:35-44, where Saul's descendants are listed again.
evidence: Say who is named as Saul's father and sons (8:33)
Say where else the line of Saul is listed (9:35-44)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} find where 1 Chronicles lists Saul's family?

topics.name: Those who lived in Jerusalem after the captivity
topics.description: Chapter 9:1-34 says all Israel was reckoned by genealogies, the people carried away to Babylon for their transgression, and lists those who first dwelt in their cities: Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, with the porters and singers and their duties.
evidence: Say why Judah was carried to Babylon (9:1)
Name the groups who lived in Jerusalem (9:2-3)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what 1 Chronicles 9 says about the people who lived in Jerusalem?

topics.name: Saul dies at Gilboa
topics.description: The Philistines fight Israel, Saul and his sons die, and the Philistines strip Saul and fasten his head in the temple of Dagon; the men of Jabesh-gilead bury him. The text says Saul died for his transgression and for not enquiring of the LORD, and the kingdom was turned to David.
evidence: Say why the writer says Saul died (10:13-14)
Say what happened to Saul's body and who buried it
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why 1 Chronicles says Saul died and what happened to the kingdom?

topics.name: David is made king and takes Jerusalem
topics.description: All Israel gathers to David at Hebron and he makes a covenant with the elders before the LORD; David and Israel take Jebus (Jerusalem) from the Jebusites, Joab leading, and David dwells there; he grows greater because the LORD of hosts was with him.
evidence: Say who came to Hebron and what they said (11:1-3)
Say who went up first against the Jebusites (11:6)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how David became king over all Israel and took Jerusalem?

topics.name: David's mighty men
topics.description: The chief of David's mighty men are named with their deeds: Jashobeam, Eleazar, Abishai and Benaiah, three men who brought David water from the well of Bethlehem (which he poured out to the LORD), and a list of other valiant men.
evidence: Say what David did with the water from Bethlehem and why (11:17-19)
Name two of the mighty men
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell about David's mighty men and the water from Bethlehem?

topics.name: Those who came to David at Ziklag and Hebron
topics.description: Chapter 12 lists warriors from Benjamin, Gad, Judah, Manasseh and other tribes who joined David at Ziklag and in the wilderness, and then the tribal armies that came to Hebron with a perfect heart to make him king over all Israel.
evidence: Say what Amasai told David (12:18)
Say why the tribes came to Hebron (12:38)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how all Israel came to support David as king?

topics.name: The ark moved on a cart and Uzza dies
topics.description: David consults the leaders and all Israel to bring the ark of God from Kirjath-jearim; on the way Uzza puts out his hand to steady the ark and the LORD strikes him. David is afraid and leaves the ark with Obed-edom, whose house is blessed.
evidence: Retell what happened to Uzza
Say where the ark was left and how the LORD treated that house (13:13-14)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what went wrong when David first tried to bring the ark to Jerusalem?

topics.name: David established at Jerusalem and the Philistines defeated
topics.description: Hiram of Tyre sends cedar and craftsmen to David, who perceives that the LORD has confirmed him king; the Philistines come twice, David enquires of God each time, and God tells him the second time to wait for the sound in the mulberry trees, and the Philistines are beaten.
evidence: Say what David did before each battle (14:10, 14)
Say what sign God gave David (14:15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how David knew when to attack the Philistines?

topics.name: The ark is brought up to Jerusalem
topics.description: David prepares a place for the ark and says only Levites should carry it; the Levites sanctify themselves and bear it on their shoulders with the staves, singers and instruments appointed, and the ark comes to the city of David with shouting, though Michal despises David.
evidence: Say why David said only the Levites should carry the ark (15:2, 13)
Say how the ark was carried this time (15:15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how David brought the ark up properly the second time?

topics.name: The ark in its tent and the worship appointed
topics.description: The ark is set in the tent David pitched; burnt and peace offerings are made, bread is given to all Israel, and Levites are appointed to minister before the ark and praise the LORD, with Asaph and others, while Zadok and priests serve at Gibeon.
evidence: Say what David gave to the people (16:3)
Name the Levite chief appointed to sound the cymbals (16:5)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the worship David appointed once the ark was in Jerusalem?

topics.name: David's psalm of thanksgiving
topics.description: David delivers to Asaph a psalm: give thanks to the LORD, seek his face, remember his marvellous works and his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, declare his glory to the nations, for the LORD is great and above all gods, and his mercy endures for ever.
evidence: Find the lines about the covenant with Abraham and the land of Canaan (16:15-18)
Say what the psalm says about the LORD and the gods of the peoples (16:25-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell some reasons David's psalm gives for thanking the LORD?

topics.name: The LORD's promise to David's house
topics.description: David wants to build a house for the ark but the LORD tells Nathan he will build David a house: he will raise up David's seed, who will build the LORD's house, whose throne will be established for ever and to whom the LORD will be a father. David sits before the LORD, praises him and asks that the word be established.
evidence: State what the LORD promises about David's seed and throne (17:11-14)
Say how David responds in prayer (17:16-27)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what the LORD promised David in 1 Chronicles 17 and how David responded?

topics.name: David's victories and officers
topics.description: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Hadarezer of Zobah, the Syrians and Edom, and dedicates the spoil to the LORD; the text says the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went, and lists his officers.
evidence: Say who preserved David in battle (18:6, 13)
Say what David did with the silver and gold (18:11)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} summarise David's victories in 1 Chronicles 18?

topics.name: David and Ammon
topics.description: David sends messengers to console Hanun king of Ammon, who shames them; Ammon hires Syrians and Joab and Abishai defeat them, and David then defeats Syria. In the next year Joab besieges Rabbah, and giants of the Philistines are killed.
evidence: Say how Hanun treated David's servants (19:4)
Say what Joab said to Abishai before the battle (19:13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why David went to war with Ammon?

topics.name: David numbers Israel and the plague
topics.description: Satan provokes David to number Israel, Joab objects, and David confesses his sin; God sends a plague and 70,000 fall. When the angel stands over Jerusalem, David pleads to bear the punishment, buys Ornan's threshing floor, builds an altar and the LORD answers by fire.
evidence: Say what David chose among the three punishments and why (21:13)
Say what David bought and what he did there (21:24-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why David's census was sin and how the plague ended?

topics.name: David prepares for the temple and charges Solomon
topics.description: David declares the threshing floor the site of the LORD's house, gathers materials, and tells Solomon that though he himself shed much blood, a son of rest will build the house for the LORD's name and the LORD will establish his throne for ever; David commands the princes to help.
evidence: Say why David himself could not build the house (22:8)
State what the LORD promised about Solomon (22:9-10)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Solomon, not David, was to build the house, and what David prepared?

topics.name: The Levites' duties
topics.description: Old David makes Solomon king, numbers the Levites from age twenty and above, and divides them into courses to assist the sons of Aaron, as porters, singers and in the temple service, now that the LORD has given his people rest.
evidence: Name the Levite families (23:6) and some of their duties (23:28-31)
Say why they no longer carry the tabernacle (23:25-26)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the Levites were appointed to do under David?

topics.name: The divisions of the priests
topics.description: Chapter 24 lists the sons of Aaron, notes that Nadab and Abihu died childless, and divides the descendants of Eleazar and Ithamar into twenty-four courses by lot, with Zadok and Ahimelech, and lists remaining Levite heads.
evidence: Say how the courses were assigned (24:5, 31)
Name the sons of Aaron who had no children (24:2)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} say how David organised the priests?

topics.name: The singers of the temple
topics.description: David and the captains set apart the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun for the service of prophesying with harps, psalteries and cymbals, in twenty-four courses by lot.
evidence: Name the three families of singers (25:1)
Say how their duties were assigned (25:8)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain who the temple singers were and how they served?

topics.name: Gatekeepers and treasurers
topics.description: Chapter 26 lists the courses of the porters at the gates of the house of the LORD, the Levites over its treasuries and dedicated things, and officers and judges for outward business.
evidence: Say what the porters did (26:12-19)
Say what the treasurers kept (26:20-28)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe the gatekeepers and treasurers David appointed?

topics.name: The monthly army and tribal leaders
topics.description: Chapter 27 lists the twelve divisions of 24,000 men that served the king by month, the tribal princes, David's stewards and counsellors, and notes that David did not number those under twenty because the LORD had said he would multiply Israel.
evidence: Say how the army was organised through the year (27:1)
Name the people who counselled David (27:32-34)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how David's army and officers were organised?

topics.name: David's charge to Solomon and the assembly
topics.description: David assembles Israel's leaders, says God did not let him build because he was a man of war, chose him as king for ever and Solomon as successor; he charges Solomon to know and serve God, and gives him the plans for the temple, telling him to be strong.
evidence: State what David says God chose (28:4-6) and the condition he gives (28:7-9)
Say what David gave to Solomon (28:11-19)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what David told Solomon and the leaders about the house of God?

topics.name: The offerings, David's prayer and Solomon enthroned
topics.description: David gives his own treasure for the house, the leaders give willingly, and David blesses the LORD before the assembly, saying all things come of him, and prays for Solomon. Solomon is made king a second time and sits on the LORD's throne; David dies full of days, riches and honour after reigning forty years.
evidence: Say what David says about giving (29:14-16)
Say how long David reigned (29:27) and who succeeded him
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how David and the people gave to the house of the LORD, and how the book ends?

topics.name: 2 Chronicles: overview
topics.description: 2 Chronicles tells of Solomon's wisdom and the temple (chs. 1-9), then the kings of Judah from Rehoboam to Zedekiah, with attention to temple worship, reform and returning to the LORD, ending with the exile and Cyrus's decree to rebuild the house (ch. 36).
evidence: Say that the book follows Solomon's temple and then the kings of Judah
Say how it ends (36:22-23, Cyrus of Persia)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline 2 Chronicles in order, from Solomon's temple to Cyrus's decree?

topics.name: Solomon's wisdom and wealth
topics.description: Solomon and the congregation go to the high place at Gibeon, where the LORD appears and tells him to ask; he asks for wisdom and knowledge to judge God's people and, because he did not ask for riches, God gives him wisdom, knowledge, riches, wealth and honour.
evidence: Say what Solomon asked and what God added (1:10-12)
Describe Solomon's wealth in 1:14-17
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what Solomon asked for at Gibeon and what God gave him?

topics.name: Solomon prepares to build the temple
topics.description: Solomon determines to build a house for the LORD's name, numbers workmen, and asks Huram king of Tyre for timber and a skilled craftsman; Huram answers, blessing the LORD, and sends a cunning man and the timber.
evidence: Say what Solomon asked from Huram (2:7-9)
Say how Huram responded (2:11-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon arranged workers and timber for the temple?

topics.name: Solomon builds the temple
topics.description: Solomon begins to build on Mount Moriah, where the LORD appeared to David and on the threshing floor of Ornan, in his fourth year; the house is overlaid with gold, with two cherubim in the most holy place, a veil, and two pillars named Jachin and Boaz.
evidence: Say where the temple was built (3:1)
Say what stood in the most holy house (3:10-13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe where Solomon built the temple and what was inside?

topics.name: The temple furnishings
topics.description: Solomon makes the bronze altar, the molten sea on twelve oxen, ten lavers, golden lampstands and tables, and the courts; Huram makes the bronze pieces, and everything inside is of gold.
evidence: Name some of the furnishings and what the sea was used for (4:2-6)
Say what the vessels in the temple were made of (4:7-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name some of the temple furnishings Solomon made?

topics.name: The ark is brought in and the glory fills the house
topics.description: At the feast the priests bring the ark of the covenant into the most holy place; when the singers and trumpeters praise the LORD, saying he is good and his mercy endures for ever, a cloud fills the house and the priests cannot minister because the glory of the LORD had filled it.
evidence: Say what was in the ark (5:10)
Describe what happened when the Levites praised the LORD (5:13-14)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the ark was placed in the new temple?

topics.name: Solomon blesses Israel and recalls the promise to David
topics.description: Solomon says the LORD dwells in thick darkness, blesses the congregation, and says the LORD has performed his word to David: David's son has been set on the throne and built the house, in which the ark with the LORD's covenant is placed.
evidence: Say what Solomon says the LORD promised David (6:5-9)
Say what Solomon says he has done (6:10-11)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Solomon says the LORD had promised David?

topics.name: Solomon's dedication prayer
topics.description: Kneeling before the whole congregation, Solomon praises the LORD who keeps covenant and mercy, asks that the promise to David be kept, and prays for the LORD to hear and forgive when Israel sins, is defeated, is in drought, or in captivity, and when a stranger prays toward the house.
evidence: Say what Solomon asks for if Israel repents (6:24-25, 36-39)
Find the request about the throne and David (6:16-17, 42)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} summarise Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the temple?

topics.name: Fire from heaven and the feast of dedication
topics.description: When Solomon finishes praying, fire comes down from heaven and consumes the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD fills the house; the people bow and praise, great sacrifices are offered, and they keep the dedication for seven days.
evidence: Describe what fell from heaven and how the people responded (7:1-3)
Say how many days they kept the feast (7:8-9)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Solomon prayed at the dedication?

topics.name: The LORD answers Solomon
topics.description: The LORD appears to Solomon by night and says that if his people humble themselves, pray, seek his face and turn from their wicked ways he will hear, forgive and heal their land; he will establish Solomon's throne as he covenanted with David, but if they forsake him he will pluck them out of the land and cast out the house.
evidence: State the condition and promise of 7:14
Say what the LORD warns will happen if they serve other gods (7:19-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Solomon about humbling themselves and about forsaking him?

topics.name: Solomon's cities, worship and ships
topics.description: Solomon builds cities, sets forced labour on the remaining peoples, keeps the burnt offerings and feasts as appointed, and orders the priests and Levites as David commanded; ships brought gold from Ophir.
evidence: Say how Solomon followed David's order for the priests and Levites (8:14-15)
Say what the ships brought (8:17-18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Solomon kept worship in order after the temple was built?

topics.name: The queen of Sheba and the end of Solomon's reign
topics.description: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with hard questions and blesses the LORD for setting him on the throne; the chapter describes his gold, throne, ships and wisdom, and ends with his forty-year reign and burial in the city of David.
evidence: Say what the queen said about the LORD (9:8)
State how long Solomon reigned (9:30)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why the queen of Sheba came and how Solomon's reign ended?

topics.name: Israel rebels against Rehoboam
topics.description: At Shechem Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's yoke; he rejects the old men's counsel and answers roughly, and Israel rebels against the house of David, while Rehoboam reigns over the cities of Judah. The text says the cause was of God.
evidence: Compare what the old men and the young men advised (10:7-11)
Say what Israel said when the king answered roughly (10:16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the northern tribes broke from Rehoboam?

topics.name: Rehoboam strengthens Judah
topics.description: Rehoboam gathers an army to fight Israel but obeys the word of Shemaiah and returns; he fortifies cities, and priests and Levites and those who set their hearts to seek the LORD come to Judah from Jeroboam's kingdom.
evidence: Say why Rehoboam did not fight Israel (11:2-4)
Say why the Levites came to Judah (11:13-16)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why Rehoboam did not go to war and why the priests and Levites came to Judah?

topics.name: Shishak and Rehoboam humbles himself
topics.description: When Rehoboam is strong he forsakes the law of the LORD, and in his fifth year Shishak of Egypt comes against Jerusalem; Shemaiah tells them the LORD has left them, and when they humble themselves the LORD grants some deliverance, though they become Shishak's servants.
evidence: Say what turned Judah to humility (12:5-7)
Say what Shishak took (12:9)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Shishak came and how the LORD responded when Rehoboam humbled himself?

topics.name: Abijah defeats Jeroboam
topics.description: Abijah of Judah, standing on Mount Zemaraim, tells Jeroboam that the LORD gave the kingdom to David and his sons by a covenant of salt, that Judah has not forsaken the LORD while Israel has made golden calves; Judah cries to the LORD and Israel is defeated.
evidence: Find the phrase about the covenant of salt (13:5)
Say why Judah prevailed (13:18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Abijah said about David and why Judah won?

topics.name: Asa removes idols and defeats Zerah
topics.description: Asa does good and right in the LORD's eyes, removes altars and high places, builds fenced cities during ten years of quiet, and when Zerah the Ethiopian comes with a huge host he cries to the LORD, saying it is nothing with him to help, and the LORD smites the Ethiopians.
evidence: Say what Asa prayed before the battle (14:11)
Say what Asa removed from Judah (14:3-5)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Asa prayed and what happened to Zerah's army?

topics.name: Azariah's warning and Asa's covenant
topics.description: The Spirit of God comes on Azariah, who tells Asa that the LORD is with them while they are with him; Asa removes the idols, renews the altar, and Judah enters a covenant to seek the LORD with all their heart and soul, and he removes his mother Maachah from being queen.
evidence: State Azariah's message (15:2)
Say what the covenant was and what it required (15:12-13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Azariah told Asa and what covenant Judah made?

topics.name: Asa relies on Syria and not the LORD
topics.description: In Asa's thirty-sixth year Baasha of Israel builds Ramah, and Asa takes treasures from the temple to hire Benhadad of Syria; Hanani the seer rebukes him for not relying on the LORD, and Asa imprisons him. In his illness he seeks physicians and not the LORD.
evidence: Say what Hanani told Asa (16:7-9)
Say how Asa responded to Hanani and in his disease (16:10, 12)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Asa's trust changed late in his reign?

topics.name: Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah
topics.description: Jehoshaphat walks in the first ways of David and seeks the LORD, not Baalim; the LORD establishes his kingdom, and in the third year of his reign he sends princes, Levites and priests with the book of the law to teach through Judah's cities, so that fear of the LORD falls on the nations.
evidence: Say what Jehoshaphat sent teachers to do (17:7-9)
Say what the LORD did for Jehoshaphat (17:5, 10)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Jehoshaphat taught Judah the law of the LORD?

topics.name: Jehoshaphat joins Ahab and Micaiah warns
topics.description: Jehoshaphat allies with Ahab and goes to Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets say go, but Micaiah, after saying he will speak what God says, shows a lying spirit sent into the prophets' mouths. Ahab disguises himself but is struck by a random arrow and dies, while Jehoshaphat cries out and God helps him.
evidence: Compare Micaiah with the four hundred prophets
Say how Ahab died and how Jehoshaphat was saved (18:30-34, 31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Jehoshaphat went with Ahab and what Micaiah said?

topics.name: Jehu's rebuke and Jehoshaphat's reforms
topics.description: Jehu the seer rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping the ungodly yet notes the good in him; Jehoshaphat goes among the people turning them back to the LORD and sets judges in the fenced cities and in Jerusalem, telling them to judge for the LORD and fear him.
evidence: Say what Jehoshaphat told the judges (19:6-7)
Say what Jehu the seer said was good in him (19:3)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Jehoshaphat set up judges and what he told them?

topics.name: The LORD fights for Judah against Moab and Ammon
topics.description: A great multitude of Moab, Ammon and Mount Seir comes against Jehoshaphat, who proclaims a fast and prays that they have no might and their eyes are on God; Jahaziel says the battle is not theirs but God's, singers go before the army, and the LORD sets the enemy against each other.
evidence: Quote the way Jahaziel describes the battle (20:15)
Describe how Judah went out to battle (20:20-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Judah won the battle against Moab and Ammon without fighting?

topics.name: The end of Jehoshaphat's reign
topics.description: Jehoshaphat walks in Asa's way, though the high places remain; he joins Ahaziah of Israel to build ships at Ezion-geber and Eliezer prophesies that the LORD has broken his works, and the ships do not sail.
evidence: Say what remained despite his good reign (20:33)
Say why the ships were broken (20:37)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why Jehoshaphat's ships were broken?

topics.name: Jehoram of Judah
topics.description: Jehoram kills his brothers, walks as the house of Ahab did (for Ahab's daughter is his wife), yet the LORD does not destroy David's house because of his covenant with David. Elijah writes warning of plague and a disease of his bowels, and Jehoram dies of it.
evidence: Say why the LORD did not destroy David's house (21:7)
Say what Elijah's writing announced (21:12-15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why God spared the house of David despite Jehoram?

topics.name: Ahaziah, Athaliah and the hidden Joash
topics.description: Ahaziah of Judah follows the counsel of Ahab's house and is killed with Joram of Israel by Jehu; Athaliah destroys the royal seed but Jehoshabeath hides the baby Joash in the house of God for six years.
evidence: Say who walked with Ahaziah and what happened to him (22:3-9)
Say who saved Joash and where he was hidden (22:11-12)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Joash escaped Athaliah?

topics.name: Jehoiada crowns Joash and Athaliah is slain
topics.description: In the seventh year Jehoiada makes a covenant with the captains, brings out the king's son in the temple with guards and Levites, anoints him, and Athaliah is put to death; Jehoiada makes a covenant between the LORD, the people and the king, and the house of Baal is destroyed.
evidence: Say how Joash was crowned and who protected him (23:1-11)
State what the king's son reigning is said to fulfil (23:3)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} retell how Joash became king and how the people renewed their covenant?

topics.name: Joash repairs the temple, then turns away
topics.description: Joash repairs the house of the LORD with money collected in a chest, but after Jehoiada dies the princes lead him to serve idols; when Zechariah the priest warns them, Joash has him stoned in the temple court, and Joash is later struck down by Syrians and conspirators.
evidence: Say how the temple was repaired (24:8-14)
Say what Joash did after Jehoiada's death (24:17-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Joash did well while Jehoiada lived and what changed after he died?

topics.name: Amaziah of Judah
topics.description: Amaziah obeys the law about not killing children for fathers' sins, sends away hired Israelite troops at a prophet's word and defeats Edom, but then brings home Edom's gods and worships them. He ignores the prophet, challenges Joash of Israel and loses at Beth-shemesh, and is later killed in a conspiracy.
evidence: Say what Amaziah did after defeating Edom (25:14)
Say why God was angry and what resulted (25:15-24)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Amaziah went from obeying the LORD to worshipping idols?

topics.name: Uzziah's strength and pride
topics.description: Uzziah seeks God while Zechariah teaches him, and God makes him prosper with victories, buildings and an army; when he is strong his heart is lifted up, he enters the temple to burn incense, and the LORD strikes him with leprosy until his death.
evidence: Say what led to Uzziah's success (26:5)
Say what he did to bring leprosy on himself (26:16-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Uzziah when he became strong?

topics.name: Jotham of Judah
topics.description: Jotham does right as Uzziah did, but does not enter the temple; he builds in Jerusalem and Judah, conquers Ammon, and becomes mighty because he prepared his ways before the LORD.
evidence: Say why Jotham became mighty (27:6)
Name something he built or won
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what made Jotham a strong king?

topics.name: Ahaz and Judah's defeat
topics.description: Ahaz walks in the ways of Israel's kings, makes images for Baalim and burns his children; the LORD delivers him to Syria and Israel, where Pekah kills many in Judah in one day. In his distress he sends to Assyria, who does not help, and he closes the temple and sets up altars everywhere.
evidence: List what Ahaz did instead of seeking the LORD (28:2-4, 22-25)
Say what happened when he turned to Assyria (28:20-21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Ahaz responded to his troubles and what happened?

topics.name: Oded and the captives sent home
topics.description: When Israel brings home 200,000 captives from Judah, the prophet Oded meets the army and says they also have sins and must send them back; some Ephraimite leaders agree, and clothe, feed and carry the captives to Jericho.
evidence: Say what Oded told the army (28:9-11)
Describe how the leaders cared for the captives (28:15)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Israelites showed kindness to the captives from Judah?

topics.name: Hezekiah cleanses and reopens the temple
topics.description: Hezekiah reopens the doors of the LORD's house in his first year, calls the priests and Levites to sanctify it and carry out the filth, and says he intends to make a covenant with the LORD; sin offerings are made for the kingdom and the sanctuary, and worship with singing and instruments resumes.
evidence: Say what Hezekiah told the Levites (29:5-11)
Describe how worship was restored (29:25-30)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah restored worship in the temple?

topics.name: Hezekiah's Passover
topics.description: Hezekiah sends letters to all Israel and Judah, including Ephraim and Manasseh, to come to Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the LORD, in the second month; some mock but many humble themselves and come, and the people keep the feast with great joy for fourteen days. Hezekiah prays for those who were not cleansed and the LORD heals the people.
evidence: Say whom Hezekiah invited (30:1-9)
Say what Hezekiah prayed for the uncleansed (30:18-20)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Hezekiah invited all Israel to the Passover and how the people responded?

topics.name: Hezekiah organises the offerings and priests
topics.description: After the Passover Israel breaks down the idols, Hezekiah appoints the priests and Levites to their courses, and the people bring tithes and firstfruits in abundance; storerooms are prepared and men are appointed to distribute. The text says Hezekiah did this with all his heart and prospered.
evidence: Say what the people brought (31:5-6)
Say how Hezekiah served God according to 31:20-21
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe how Hezekiah arranged for the support of the priests and Levites?

topics.name: Sennacherib threatens and the LORD delivers Jerusalem
topics.description: Sennacherib invades Judah; Hezekiah strengthens Jerusalem and tells the people there is more with them than with the king of Assyria. Sennacherib's servants mock the LORD, Hezekiah and Isaiah pray, and the LORD sends an angel to cut off the Assyrian leaders; Sennacherib goes home and his sons kill him.
evidence: Say what Hezekiah told the people (32:7-8)
Say what the LORD did after Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed (32:20-22)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Hezekiah and Isaiah prayed when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem, and what God did?

topics.name: Hezekiah's illness, pride and death
topics.description: Hezekiah is sick to death and prays and is given a sign, but his heart is lifted up and wrath falls on Judah until he and Jerusalem humble themselves. He prospers, stops the upper watercourse of Gihon, and when envoys come from Babylon God leaves him to test what was in his heart; he dies and is honoured in burial.
evidence: Say what happened because of Hezekiah's pride and how it was turned aside (32:25-26)
