Name something Hezekiah built for Jerusalem (32:30)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how Hezekiah's heart was tested and what the LORD did?

topics.name: Manasseh's repentance and Amon
topics.description: Manasseh rebuilds the high places and sets idols in the house of God; the LORD brings Assyria's captains, who take him in fetters to Babylon, and there he humbles himself, prays and is restored to Jerusalem, where he removes the idols and repairs the altar. His son Amon does evil and does not humble himself, and is killed by his servants.
evidence: Say what happened to Manasseh in affliction and what he did after returning (33:11-16)
Say how Amon differed from his father (33:23)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Manasseh turned back to the LORD and how Amon was different?

topics.name: Josiah seeks God and purges the land
topics.description: Josiah begins to seek the God of David in his eighth year, and in his twelfth year purges Judah and Jerusalem of high places, groves and images, and also in Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon and Naphtali; in his eighteenth year he sends Shaphan and others to repair the house of the LORD.
evidence: Say when Josiah began to seek God and when he began to purge (34:3)
Say who oversaw the temple repair (34:8-13)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Josiah did in the early years of his reign?

topics.name: The book of the law found and the covenant renewed
topics.description: Hilkiah finds the book of the law in the temple; Josiah tears his clothes, sends to Huldah the prophetess, who says the evil will come but not in his days because he humbled himself. Josiah reads the book to all the people and makes a covenant before the LORD to keep his commandments.
evidence: Say what Josiah did when the book was read (34:19)
Say what Huldah told him and what covenant he made (34:23-31)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the book of the law was found and what Josiah did next?

topics.name: Josiah's Passover
topics.description: Josiah keeps the Passover in Jerusalem on the fourteenth of the first month, appointing priests and Levites to their duties, giving offerings to the people, with the singers in their places as David commanded; no Passover like it had been kept in Israel since Samuel.
evidence: Say how Josiah organised the Levites and priests (35:2-6)
Say how this Passover compared to earlier ones (35:18)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} describe Josiah's Passover and what made it special?

topics.name: Josiah dies at Megiddo
topics.description: Pharaoh Necho goes up to fight at Carchemish and warns Josiah not to meddle, saying God commanded him; Josiah does not heed and goes out to fight at Megiddo, where archers wound him, and he dies; all Judah mourns, and Jeremiah laments for him.
evidence: Say what Necho told Josiah (35:21)
Say what Josiah did and what happened (35:22-24)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how Josiah died and who mourned for him?

topics.name: Judah's last kings
topics.description: Jehoahaz is deposed by the king of Egypt, Jehoiakim is bound by Nebuchadnezzar and temple vessels are taken to Babylon; Jehoiachin is taken to Babylon, and Zedekiah rebels, hardens his heart, and with the priests and people pollutes the house of the LORD.
evidence: Say what Nebuchadnezzar took to Babylon (36:7, 10)
Say how Zedekiah and the people sinned (36:12-14)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} name Judah's last kings in order and say what happened to each?

topics.name: The LORD sends Judah into exile
topics.description: The LORD sent messengers to his people because of his compassion, but they mocked the prophets until there was no remedy; the Chaldeans burn the house of God, break down Jerusalem's wall, and carry the survivors to Babylon until the land enjoyed its sabbaths, seventy years, as Jeremiah spoke.
evidence: Say why the LORD sent the messengers and how they were treated (36:15-16)
Say what the seventy years were to fulfil (36:21)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Judah went into exile according to 2 Chronicles 36?

topics.name: Cyrus's decree
topics.description: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia the LORD stirs up his spirit to proclaim that the LORD God of heaven has charged him to build him a house in Jerusalem, and invites any of his people to go up.
evidence: Say whose spirit the LORD stirred up and what he proclaimed
Say how 2 Chronicles ends
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain how 2 Chronicles closes and what Cyrus announced?

topics.name: Ezra: overview
topics.description: Ezra reports the return from Babylon under Cyrus and Zerubbabel and the rebuilding of the temple despite opposition (chs. 1-6), then Ezra's own journey to Jerusalem, his prayer over intermarriage, and the people's covenant to put away foreign wives (chs. 7-10).
evidence: Name the two parts: the return and temple under Zerubbabel, and Ezra's mission
Say how the book begins (Cyrus) and ends (the list of those with foreign wives)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} outline Ezra, from Cyrus's decree to the people's confession?

topics.name: Cyrus's decree and the first return
topics.description: In the first year of Cyrus the LORD stirs his spirit, and he proclaims that the LORD God of heaven charged him to build a house in Jerusalem and invites any of God's people to go up. Those whose spirit God raised go, neighbours help them, and Cyrus brings out the temple vessels to Sheshbazzar.
evidence: Say whose word was being fulfilled (1:1)
Say what Cyrus returned to Sheshbazzar (1:7-11)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain what Cyrus decreed and who went up to Jerusalem?

topics.name: The list of those who returned
topics.description: Chapter 2 lists those who came up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua by family and town, then priests, Levites, singers, porters and temple servants, notes some who could not prove their ancestry, and gives the total and the freewill gifts for the house.
evidence: Say who led the group (2:2)
Say what some of the chief fathers gave (2:68-69)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Ezra records the names and numbers of the returnees?

topics.name: The altar is rebuilt and worship begins
topics.description: In the seventh month the people gather at Jerusalem; Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar of the God of Israel, offer burnt offerings morning and evening as written in the law of Moses, and keep the feast of tabernacles, although fear was on them because of the people of the lands.
evidence: Say what they built first and why (3:2-3)
Name the feast they kept (3:4)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why the returned exiles began by building the altar?

topics.name: The foundation of the temple is laid
topics.description: In the second year the builders lay the foundation, with priests and Levites praising the LORD according to David's order; the people shout for joy, while many old men who had seen the first house weep, so that joy and weeping cannot be told apart.
evidence: Describe what the people sang (3:11)
Say why some of the old men wept (3:12)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell why some people shouted for joy and some wept when the foundation was laid?

topics.name: The adversaries offer to help and then oppose
topics.description: The adversaries of Judah and Benjamin ask to build with Zerubbabel, claiming they seek his God; Zerubbabel and Jeshua refuse, saying they must build alone as Cyrus commanded, and the people of the land weaken their hands and hire counsellors against them.
evidence: Say what the adversaries asked and what the leaders answered (4:2-3)
Say how they opposed the work (4:4-5)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} explain why Zerubbabel refused the offer to help build the temple?

topics.name: Letters to the king and the work stops
topics.description: Later accusations are written against Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes; Rehum and Shimshai write to Artaxerxes that Jerusalem is a rebellious city, and the king orders the work stopped. The work on the house of God ceases until the second year of Darius.
evidence: Say what the letter claimed about Jerusalem (4:12-16)
Say how long the work ceased (4:24)
topics.prompt: Can {{name}} tell how the rebuilding was stopped and for how long?

topics.name: Haggai and Zechariah and the resumed work
topics.description: Haggai and Zechariah prophesy to the Jews in the name of the God of Israel, and Zerubbabel and Jeshua rise and begin to build again; when Tatnai the governor asks who commanded it, the text says the eye of their God was on the elders.
evidence: Name the prophets and the leaders who began again (5:1-2)
Say what kept the work going when Tatnai questioned them (5:5)

topics.description: Nehemiah, in Shushan in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, hears from Hanani that the remnant in Judah is in affliction and Jerusalem's wall is broken down; he weeps, fasts and prays, confessing sin, recalling the LORD's word to Moses about scattering and gathering, and asks for mercy before the king.

15:1 gives Azariah's accession in the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam of Israel (see 14:23)
Chapter 15 gives the kings of Israel in the years of Azariah of Judah (15:8, 13, 17, 23, 27)
Ahaz is Jotham's son (16:1; 15:38), and the enemies Rezin and Pekah were sent against Judah in Jotham's days (15:37)
Hoshea killed Pekah in 15:30 and reigns in Samaria in 17:1
17:7 begins "for so it was" and explains the captivity reported in 17:6
17:24 follows the carrying away of Israel (17:23) and describes who replaced them
Hezekiah is Ahaz's son (16:20) and reigns in the third year of Hoshea (18:1), around the fall of Samaria (18:9-12)
18:13 happens in the fourteenth year of Hezekiah, the king described in 18:1-8
19:1-4 begins when Hezekiah heard Rabshakeh's words from chapter 18
20:1 is "in those days" of Hezekiah, and 20:6 promises to deliver the city from Assyria's king
Manasseh is Hezekiah's son (20:21) and rebuilds the high places Hezekiah destroyed (21:3)
Josiah is Amon's son (21:26) and reigns in the aftermath of Manasseh's sins (21:11-15; 22:13)
23:1-2 gather the people to hear the book found in chapter 22
23:21 follows the reforms in 23:1-20
23:29 begins "in his days" of Josiah, whose reign 23:28 has just summarised
24:1 begins in the days of Jehoiakim, whose reign is introduced in 23:36-37
25:1 follows Zedekiah's rebellion against the king of Babylon (24:20)
25:22 speaks of the people left in Judah after the destruction in 25:1-21
1 Chronicles retells Israel's history from Adam (1:1), ending with the Babylonian captivity mentioned in 9:1 which 2 Kings 25 reports
1 Chronicles 1 is the first chapter of the book and begins the genealogies
2:1 begins with the sons of Israel, whose father Israel is in the line traced from 1:34
3:1 continues the line of Judah to David (2:15) with his sons
4:1 returns to the sons of Judah after the line of David in chapter 3
5:1 turns to Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, after the families of Judah and Simeon
6:1 begins with the sons of Levi, following the tribes of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh in chapter 5
7:1 starts with the sons of Issachar after the Levites in chapter 6
8:1 begins with Benjamin, one of the sons of Israel listed in 2:1-2
9:1 closes the genealogies of Israel by mentioning Judah's captivity to Babylon, the event with which 2 Kings 25 ends
Chapter 10 narrates the death of Saul, whose family is listed in 8:33 and 9:39-44
11:1-2 follows Saul's death and the turning of the kingdom to David (10:14)
11:10 names those who strengthened themselves with David in his kingdom, introduced in 11:1-9
Chapter 12 returns to those who came to David at Ziklag (12:1) and to Hebron (12:23-40), the place where Israel gathered in 11:1
13:1-5 begins with David consulting all Israel after all Israel had made him king (chs. 11-12)
14:1-2 follows the ark being left with Obed-edom (13:14) and states that the LORD had confirmed David as king
15:2, 13 explains the earlier failure at Uzza (13:9-10), so the ark is now carried by the Levites as God commanded
16:1 begins when they brought the ark of God into the tent, as reported at the end of chapter 15
16:7 is the psalm David delivered on the day the ark was set in the tent (16:1)
17:1 begins with David dwelling in his house of cedars while the ark is in a tent, as in 15:1 and 16:1
18:1 follows the LORD's promise to subdue David's enemies (17:10)
19:1-2 follows David's wars of chapter 18 and begins with the death of Nahash
21:1 follows David's wars (chs. 18-20) and Joab leads the counting (21:2-4)
22:1 identifies the site as the altar place bought in chapter 21 (21:26-28)
23:1 says David made Solomon king, and 23:2 gathers the Levites for the temple work prepared in chapter 22
24:1 gives the divisions of the sons of Aaron, the priests the Levites of chapter 23 serve (23:28)
25:1 follows the courses of priests and Levites and refers to Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun (6:31-44)
26:1 gives the divisions of the porters, another Levite service listed after the singers (23:5; 25:1)
27:1 turns from the Levites' service in chapters 23-26 to the king's service by Israel's captains
28:1 assembles the princes and officers listed in chapters 23-27
29:1 continues David's address to the congregation about Solomon from chapter 28
2 Chronicles begins with Solomon son of David (1:1), continuing 1 Chronicles which ends with Solomon made king (1 Chronicles 29:22-28)
2 Chronicles 1 begins at the start of Solomon's reign (1:1)
Chapter 2 follows Solomon's wealth and wisdom in chapter 1 (1:1, 12) and begins his plan to build (2:1)
Chapter 3 begins construction, for which the materials and workers were arranged in chapter 2
Chapter 4 continues the work of chapter 3, making the furniture for the house
5:1 says all the work for the house was finished before the ark is brought in
6:1 follows the cloud filling the house (5:13-14)
6:12 begins with Solomon standing before the altar after blessing the congregation (6:3-11)
7:1 begins when Solomon had made an end of praying
7:12 happens after Solomon finished the house and the dedication (7:11)
8:1 begins at the end of twenty years when Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house
Chapter 9 concludes Solomon's reign after his works in chapter 8
10:1 begins with Rehoboam, who reigns in Solomon's place after Solomon's death (9:31)
11:1 follows the division in chapter 10, as Rehoboam gathers Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel
12:1 follows Rehoboam establishing the kingdom (11:5-17, 12:1)
13:1-2 gives the reign of Abijah, Rehoboam's son (12:16), and the war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam (12:15)
14:1 begins when Abijah died and Asa his son reigned
15:1-2 speaks to Asa as he returns from the victory over Zerah in chapter 14
16:1 is in the thirty-sixth year of Asa, after the peace of 15:19 and his covenant to seek the LORD (15:12)
17:1 says Jehoshaphat reigned after Asa his father (see 16:13-14)
18:1 says Jehoshaphat had riches and honour and joined affinity with Ahab
19:1-2 follows Jehoshaphat's safe return from Ramoth-gilead and the rebuke of Jehu about helping Ahab
20:1 is "after this" the reforms and rebuke of the earlier chapters of Jehoshaphat's reign
20:31 summarises the reign of Jehoshaphat after the victory in 20:1-30
21:1 says Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and Jehoram his son reigned
22:1 says the people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king after raiders killed his older brothers (21:17; 22:1)
23:1 begins in the seventh year, after Joash was hidden six years (22:12)
24:1-2 gives the reign of Joash, the child crowned in chapter 23, doing right all the days of Jehoiada
25:1 gives Amaziah as the son of Joash, whose reign ended in chapter 24 (24:25-27)
26:1 says all the people of Judah took Uzziah and made him king in his father Amaziah's room
Jotham is Uzziah's son (27:1), and he judged the people in his father's illness (26:21)
28:1 gives Ahaz as Jotham's son and a very different king
28:8-9 reports Israel carrying away 200,000 of their brethren of Judah, which Oded confronts
29:1-3 gives Hezekiah as Ahaz's son who reopened the doors Ahaz shut (28:24; 29:3)
30:1 follows the temple being cleansed in chapter 29
31:1 says "when all this was finished" after the Passover of chapter 30
32:1 is "after these things", after Hezekiah's faithfulness in chapters 29-31
32:24 is "in those days" of Hezekiah, after the deliverance in 32:1-23
33:1 gives Manasseh as Hezekiah's son (32:33), rebuilding what Hezekiah broke down (33:3)
34:1 gives Josiah, the eight-year-old made king after Amon was killed (33:25)
34:14 happens as the temple money was brought out for the repairs begun in 34:8-13
35:1 begins "moreover" after the covenant in 34:31-32 and the removal of abominations (34:33)
35:20 says "after all this", after Josiah had prepared the temple and kept the Passover
36:1 gives Jehoahaz as Josiah's son made king after Josiah died (35:24)
36:15 sums up the judgment of the people described in 36:12-14
36:22 follows the seventy years of exile Jeremiah spoke of (36:21)
Ezra 1:1-3 repeats the decree of Cyrus with which 2 Chronicles ends (2 Chronicles 36:22-23)
Ezra 1 is the first chapter of the book and begins in the first year of Cyrus (1:1)
2:1 lists those who went up out of the captivity, whose departure was reported in 1:5
3:1 begins when the seventh month came and the people were in their cities, as at the end of chapter 2 (2:70)
3:7-8 prepares materials and starts building in the second year after the altar was set up
4:1 begins when the adversaries heard that the exiles were building the temple, whose foundation was laid in 3:10
4:6 gives later opposition against the Jews, continuing the opposition from 4:4-5 until Darius
5:1 follows the cessation until the second year of Darius (4:24)
5:6 is the letter Tatnai sent after he asked the elders who commanded the building (5:3-5)
6:1 is Darius's search ordered in response to Tatnai's request (5:17)
6:13 says Tatnai did according to what Darius sent in 6:6-12
7:1 begins "after these things", after the temple was finished in the sixth year of Darius (6:15), in the reign of Artaxerxes
7:11 gives the letter that Artaxerxes gave to Ezra, who goes up in 7:6-9
8:1 lists those who went up with Ezra from Babylon, in the reign of Artaxerxes mentioned in 7:1
8:15 describes the gathering of the company listed in 8:1-14 at the river that runs to Ahava
9:1 begins "when these things were done", after Ezra's arrival and delivery of the treasure (8:32-36)
9:5 is Ezra's prayer after he sat appalled at the report in 9:1-4
10:1 begins when Ezra had prayed and confessed (9:5-15)
10:18 lists those found among the sons of the priests and others, after the covenant in 10:3-17
Nehemiah continues the return from exile in Ezra, with Ezra himself appearing in Nehemiah 8
Nehemiah 1 is the first chapter of the book and begins in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes (1:1)
2:1 follows Nehemiah's prayer for success before the king (1:11), in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes
2:11 says Nehemiah came to Jerusalem, having been sent by the king in 2:6-9
3:1 begins the actual building of the wall that the people agreed to start in 2:18
4:1 says Sanballat heard that the wall was being built, as chapter 3 describes
5:1 describes a great cry of the people during the building described in chapters 3-4
6:1 says the enemies heard that Nehemiah had built the wall and no breach remained, continuing chapters 4-5
7:1 begins "when the wall was built", as reported in 6:15
8:1 happens when the seventh month came and the children of Israel were in their cities (7:73), after the register of chapter 7
8:13 happens on the second day after the reading of the law in 8:1-12
9:1 is the twenty-fourth day of the same month as the feast of booths in 8:14-18
9:6 is the prayer of the Levites who called on the people to bless the LORD in 9:5
10:1 sets seals on the sure covenant written in 9:38
11:1 answers the problem that the city was large but the people few (7:4)
12:1 lists those who went up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, whom Ezra 2 and Nehemiah 7 mention
12:27 is the dedication of the wall whose completion is reported in 6:15
13:1 happens "on that day" of the reading at the wall dedication (12:44, 13:1), and 13:6 reports Nehemiah returning from the king
13:15 reports "in those days" the further abuses Nehemiah found after returning to Jerusalem (13:6-7)
Esther is set in Shushan among Jews of the dispersion, in the Persian Empire where Ezra and Nehemiah also served (Esther 1:1; Nehemiah 1:1)
Esther 1 is the first chapter of the book and begins in the days of Ahasuerus (1:1)
2:1 says the king's wrath was appeased after Vashti's removal in chapter 1 and the servants propose that a new queen be sought (2:2-4)
2:19-20 say Mordecai sat in the gate and Esther was still queen, as established in 2:17
3:1 begins "after these things", after Mordecai's service to the king in chapter 2
4:1 begins when Mordecai perceived all that was done, the decree of chapter 3
5:1 is the third day, after the three-day fast Esther requested (4:16)
6:1 is "that night", after Haman's gallows was built and Esther's first banquet (5:14)
7:1 is the banquet Esther prepared for the king and Haman (5:8; 6:14)
8:1 is "on that day", the day Haman was hanged (7:10)
9:1 is the day appointed in Haman's decree (3:13), now reversed by the king's second decree (8:11-13)
9:20 follows the deliverance of 9:1-19, which Mordecai records
10:2-3 summarises Mordecai's advancement by the king, begun in 8:2, 15 and 9:4
Esther 2:5-6 says Mordecai's family was carried away from Jerusalem with Jeconiah, the captivity reported in 2 Kings 24:12-16
